45090.title: Users without view permission cannot reach the print option
provenance: This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9383 and story SV-9384 (Story 1, Print Option in More Menu) and the Printer Friendly Work Orders specification version 8, section S1-N1, read on 25 August 2026.

before.custom_preconds: 1. Sign in as a user whose role cannot view work orders, or have an administrator create one. To set a role up that way: open “Settings” from the menu behind your name at the top right, click “Roles & Permissions” in the sidebar, then click the pencil on the role in question and switch its work-order viewing permission off. Then, in the top menu, try to reach “Work Orders” at all.
before.custom_steps: 1. Attempt to open the work order detail page.
before.custom_expected:
1. You cannot access the work order detail page and therefore cannot reach the print option (enforced by existing access control).

NOTE FOR THE TESTER: this needs a sign-in that cannot open work orders at all. Ask the QA lead to set one up; until then leave the case Untested.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9383 and story SV-9384 (Story 1, Print Option in More Menu) and the Printer Friendly Work Orders specification version 8, section S1-N1, read on 25 August 2026.

AUTOMATION: READY

45097.title: No customer assigned prints an explicit placeholder
provenance: This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9383 and story SV-9385 (Story 2, Print Layout - Work Order Header) and the Printer Friendly Work Orders specification version 8, section S2-N1, read on 25 August 2026.

before.custom_preconds:
1. In the top menu click “Work Orders” and open a work order by clicking its row. On the work order’s toolbar click the three-dots button at the top right, then choose “Print Work Order”. The menu holds five items in this order: “Audit Log”, “Timesheets”, “Add Work Order Fee / Discount”, “Print Work Order”, “Delete Work Order”. Choosing it opens your browser’s own print dialog — the printout is what you are checking, so use your browser’s print preview to look at it.
2. The open work order has no customer assigned.
before.custom_steps: 1. Read the customer section of the printout.
before.custom_expected:
1. The customer section displays “No customer assigned”.

NOTE FOR THE TESTER: this needs a work order with no customer on it. Every work order on this test system has one, so the case cannot be set up here yet.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9383 and story SV-9385 (Story 2, Print Layout - Work Order Header) and the Printer Friendly Work Orders specification version 8, section S2-N1, read on 25 August 2026.

AUTOMATION: READY

45104.title: Cancelled lines still print if visible on screen
provenance: This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9383 and story SV-9386 (Story 3, Print Layout - Line Items) and the Printer Friendly Work Orders specification version 8, section S3-R6, read on 25 August 2026.

before.custom_preconds:
1. In the top menu click “Work Orders” and open a work order by clicking its row. On the work order’s toolbar click the three-dots button at the top right, then choose “Print Work Order”. The menu holds five items in this order: “Audit Log”, “Timesheets”, “Add Work Order Fee / Discount”, “Print Work Order”, “Delete Work Order”. Choosing it opens your browser’s own print dialog — the printout is what you are checking, so use your browser’s print preview to look at it.
2. The open work order has a line with a Cancelled status visible on the Lines tab.
before.custom_steps: 1. On the Print Work Order view (see Preconditions), read the printout for the cancelled line.
before.custom_expected:
1. Line items with a status of “Cancelled” still appear on the printout if they are visible on screen, with their status clearly indicated.

NOTE FOR THE TESTER: this needs a work order line whose status is Cancelled, and none of the work orders checked had one. If you can set a line to Cancelled yourself, do that and then run the case; otherwise leave it Untested.

---

45111.title: A very long tech story wraps and prints in full
provenance: This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9383 and story SV-9386 (Story 3, Print Layout - Line Items) and the Printer Friendly Work Orders specification version 8, section S3-E2, read on 25 August 2026.

before.custom_preconds:
1. In the top menu click “Work Orders” and open a work order by clicking its row. On the work order’s toolbar click the three-dots button at the top right, then choose “Print Work Order”. The menu holds five items in this order: “Audit Log”, “Timesheets”, “Add Work Order Fee / Discount”, “Print Work Order”, “Delete Work Order”. Choosing it opens your browser’s own print dialog — the printout is what you are checking, so use your browser’s print preview to look at it.
2. At least one line on the open work order has a tech story of 500 or more characters.
before.custom_steps: 1. On the Print Work Order view (see Preconditions), read the long tech story on the printout.
before.custom_expected:
1. The tech story wraps and prints in full; it is not truncated.

NOTE FOR THE TESTER: this needs a tech story of at least 500 characters - about a full paragraph. If you can paste that much text into a line’s tech story, do that and then run the case; otherwise leave it Untested.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9383 and story SV-9386 (Story 3, Print Layout - Line Items) and the Printer Friendly Work Orders specification version 8, section S3-E2, read on 25 August 2026.
